detail:
The National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) describes generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) as a persistent feeling of anxiety or dread that interferes with daily life. NIMH notes that people with GAD feel extremely worried or nervous more frequently or more intensely about everyday things, even when the worry is out of proportion to the situation, and that the feelings can last for months or years. The disorder develops gradually and usually starts in early adulthood, although NIMH notes it can occur at any age.

NIMH describes diagnosis as requiring difficulty controlling worry on most days for at least 6 months, together with symptoms that can include feeling restless or on edge, fatigue, trouble concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, and problems with sleep. The exact cause is described as unknown, with research suggesting a mix of genetics, brain chemistry, biology, and environment, and NIMH notes GAD may run in families. Treatment in the sources typically involves psychotherapy, medication, or both, with cognitive behavioral therapy described as a research-supported type of psychotherapy commonly used for GAD.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about generalized anxiety disorder symptoms and treatment options.
summary: NIMH describes generalized anxiety disorder as persistent, hard-to-control worry about everyday things lasting months or years, diagnosed from worry on most days for at least 6 months plus symptoms such as restlessness, fatigue, and muscle tension.

symptoms can include restlessness, fatigue, muscle tension, and sleep problems
title: Generalized anxiety disorder: persistent worry that is hard to control
